This course introduces the ideas of data summary and visualization, probability, and statistics with applications to natural and social sciences and daily life. Topics include but not limited to: random variables, discrete and continuous probability distributions, sampling distributions, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, analysis of variance, and linear regression. This course builds a foundation for statistical inference, machine learning, and data modeling.

The course will assume facility with using the internet and a personal computer. A portion of the course involves [\textsf{R}](https://www.r-project.org/about.html) programming using [RStudio or Posit Cloud](https://posit.cloud/), but prior coding experience is not required.

### Learning outcomes

By the end of the course, students will be able to:

- **Statistical reasoning and communication**
Students will be able to interpret data and statistical results in context, clearly communicating conclusions, uncertainty, and practical significance.

- **Core probability and sampling foundations**
Students will be able to use basic probability concepts and sampling distribution ideas (including the central limit theorem) to justify and explain common statistical methods.

- **Statistical inference for common parameters**
Students will be able to construct and interpret confidence intervals and hypothesis tests for key parameters (including means, proportions, and comparisons across groups), stating assumptions and limitations.

- **Modeling and analysis using R**
Students will be able to use R to perform reproducible statistical analyses, including visualization, regression modeling, and model assessment, and to document work appropriately (including responsible AI support when permitted).
